prompt.provenance_instruction: Answer the following question about Drosophila neuroscience. For every claim you make, state where the information comes from - for example: the specific database, dataset, or tool query you used; the publication (with full citation); or your general training knowledge. If you are uncertain or do not have a source, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The calyx is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents. The pedunculus is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: There are several types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain, including [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes. VFB holds records of [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are projection neurons from the antennal lobe and sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx.

results.title: Gene expression
results.question: What neurotransmitter do mushroom body Kenyon cells use?
results.response: Mushroom body Kenyon cells, such as alpha/beta core Kenyon cells, use acetylcholine as a neurotransmitter. VFB does not currently hold data on other neurotransmitters used by these cells.

results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. More specifically, it connects to the mushroom body calyx and lateral horn.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
Approximately more than 125,000 neurons.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions such as navigation and orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal and memory-related behaviours.

results.question: What genetic tools are commonly used to label mushroom body neurons in Drosophila?
results.response: Genetic tools such as [PBac{544.SVS-1}Bsg[CPTI100062] expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBti0143545 "Open PBac{544.SVS-1}Bsg[CPTI100062] expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [PBac{566.P.SVS-1}Bsg[CPTI100005] expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBti0143520 "Open PBac{566.P.SVS-1}Bsg[CPTI100005] expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [PBac{602.P.SVS-1}Fas2[CPTI000483] expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBti0144014 "Open PBac{602.P.SVS-1}Fas2[CPTI000483] expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain") are used to label neurons in Drosophila. [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") is a type of neuron found in the mushroom body. VFB does not currently hold data on which of these tools specifically label mushroom body neurons, including Kenyon cell.

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response:
Dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons comes from specific types of dopaminergic neurons. The dopaminergic PPL1 neuron provides input to the adult [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons also comes from dopaminergic PAM neuron 6. 

The evidence does not specify which DAN types connect to which MBON types, as this part of the question is unanswered.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind and has distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer. This arrangement allows it to detect looming stimuli. Its activity elicits a jump escape response. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. The lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. There are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and they are cholinergic. The dendritic arbors of the lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells.

results.title: Comparative anatomy
results.question: How does the organisation of the antennal lobe compare between adult and larval Drosophila?
results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") compares between adult and larval Drosophila in terms of glomerular organization, with the adult having approximately 50 glomeruli and the larval having around 22 glomeruli.

results.response: Publications describing the dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and their role in aversive memory include Claridge-Chang et al., 2009, Mao and Davis, 2009, Budnik and White, 1988, and Ren et al., 2016.

results.title: Upstream circuit
results.question: What sensory neurons provide input to the fan-shaped body, and through how many synaptic steps?
results.response: The [fan-shaped body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003679 "Open fan-shaped body in Virtual Fly Brain") receives input from various sensory neurons. VFB holds [229](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003679,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in fan-shaped body") neuron types with a part in or for the fan-shaped body. The exact number of synaptic steps between these sensory neurons and the fan-shaped body is not specified.

results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?
results.response: There are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons. VFB has annotated 5 reciprocal class-level pairs between these two neuron types. The target-to-source weight pairwise connections for these pairs is 35.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response: A pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn involves intermediate neuron types. Antennal lobe projection neurons are intermediate neuron types between olfactory receptor neurons and the lateral horn. The connections are from olfactory receptor neurons to antennal lobe projection neurons, and then from antennal lobe projection neurons to the lateral horn. VFB does not currently hold data on other intermediate neuron types in this pathway.

results.title: Cell type taxonomy depth
results.question: How many distinct neuron types are currently classified within the adult Drosophila visual system, and how are they organised hierarchically?
results.response: The adult brain contains 11491 distinct neuron types. Classification of neuron types includes subtypes, with more than 1000 matches for subclasses of visual system neuron. However, the hierarchical organisation of these neuron types is not specified.

results.title: Connectivity strength comparison
results.question: Which neuron type provides the strongest synaptic input to the MBON-gamma1pedc>a/b neuron, and how does this compare to the next strongest inputs?
results.response: VFB does not currently hold data on the strongest synaptic input to the MBON-gamma1pedc>a/b neuron. However, for [mushroom body output neuron 11](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100246 "Open mushroom body output neuron 11 in Virtual Fly Brain"), VFB holds records on upstream connectivity classes, which could potentially provide insight into synaptic inputs. VFB also holds records on downstream connectivity classes for mushroom body output neuron 11.

results.title: Shared connectivity
results.question: Do the alpha/beta and gamma Kenyon cells converge on any of the same downstream MBON types? Which MBONs receive input from both?
results.response: The [alpha/beta Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100248 "Open alpha/beta Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") converge on some of the same downstream [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") types. VFB does not currently hold data on which specific mushroom body output neurons receive input from both alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells.

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response: The anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure is: DA1 glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. Alternatively, a more detailed hierarchy is: DA1 glomerulus -> adult olfactory antennal lobe glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain.

results.title: Cross-region connectivity
results.question: What neuron types connect the central complex to the lateral accessory lobe, and how strong are these connections?
results.response: Neurons that connect the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") to the [lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00050314 "Open lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018 in Virtual Fly Brain") include [PFL1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111433 "Open PFL1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [PFL2_PB4](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111453 "Open PFL2_PB4 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [PFL3_PB7](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111450 "Open PFL3_PB7 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [PFL1_PB1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111434 "Open PFL1_PB1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [PFL1_PB7](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111440 "Open PFL1_PB7 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [PFL1_PB2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111435 "Open PFL1_PB2 in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB does not currently hold data on the strength of these connections.

results.title: Dataset coverage
results.question: For the DNa02 descending neuron type, what data is available in VFB? Is it in the Hemibrain, FAFB, or both? Are there light microscopy images and driver lines?
results.response: Data for [descending neuron of the anterior dorsal brain DNa02](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047573 "Open descending neuron of the anterior dorsal brain DNa02 in Virtual Fly Brain") is available, including light microscopy images and driver lines. VFB holds [18](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047573,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNa02") images of DNa02 and there are [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047573,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNa02") transgene expression reports. Genetic tools are available to label DNa02 descending neuron. VFB does not currently hold data on whether DNa02 is in the Hemibrain or FAFB, or both.

results.question: I want to study the neural circuit underlying CO2 avoidance in Drosophila. What neurons are involved, how are they connected, and what genetic tools can I use to access them?
results.response: The neurons involved in the detection of carbon dioxide are carbon dioxide sensitive neurons. These neurons are involved in the detection of carbon dioxide. The connectivity of these neurons is not specified. Genetic tools to access these neurons are not specified.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response: The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. It is a [primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047097 "Open primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB holds records showing the giant fiber neuron has connections with various neuron types, including [adult VNC neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00059289 "Open adult VNC neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [thoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001983 "Open thoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047096 "Open secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch OFF hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049540 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [mesothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001985 "Open mesothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), primary neuron, [Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049542 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [prothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001984 "Open prothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049539 "Open Notch ON hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB2-4 lineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048927 "Open NB2-4 lineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049541 "Open Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). The giant fiber neuron's anatomy and connectivity make it a subject of interest for study using genetic tools. Relevant publications include those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Allen et al. (1998), Dorkenwald et al. (2024), and Schlegel et al. (2024). VFB does not currently hold data on available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response: Neuron types that might mediate a connection between the visual system and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") include projection neurons and visual projection neurons. Adult visual projection neurons to the mushroom body have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. This suggests that visual information can reach the memory circuit via these neurons.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration
results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response: The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") suggests that temperature information could influence memory formation. Thermosensory projection neurons relay temperature-detecting neurons to higher brain centers, and connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body is supported, including connections to mushroom-body-associated dopaminergic neurons and gamma main Kenyon cells. VFB holds records for several neuron types, including [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [projection neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007392 "Open projection neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [local neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051493 "Open local neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), which may be relevant to understanding thermosensory influence on mushroom-body memory circuitry.

results.title: Data availability survey
results.question: I'm interested in studying the subesophageal zone (SEZ). How well-characterised is this region in VFB? What neuron types are annotated, what connectomics data is available, and what genetic tools exist for SEZ neurons?
results.response: The [subesophageal zone](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051068 "Open subesophageal zone in Virtual Fly Brain") is characterised with available imagery and various query options for neuron types, parts, subclasses, and transgene expression. There are genetic tools for subesophageal zone neurons, including GAL4 drivers and binary/intersectional drivers. VFB holds [4205](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00051068,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in subesophageal zone") genetic tool/expression pattern rows for the subesophageal zone, with examples including [P{GMR12D05-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0057511 "Open P{GMR12D05-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{GMR16C05-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0057869 "Open P{GMR16C05-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), and P{VT000003-GAL4} expression pattern. VFB does not currently hold data on the specific neuron types annotated in the subesophageal zone or the available connectomics data.

results.title: Graph view regression - medulla region connectivity
results.question: what are the class summarised connectivity from the medulla in graph form
results.response: The [medulla](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003748 "Open medulla in Virtual Fly Brain") has connections with neurons that have presynaptic terminals, postsynaptic terminals, and synaptic terminals within it. It is also innervated by tracts and nerves, and has parts and subclasses. Neurons with some part in the medulla are connected to it, and there is transgene expression in the medulla. VFB does not currently hold data on a class summarised connectivity graph of the medulla in a specific format, but it does record various types of connections to and from the medulla.

results.title: Project identity
results.question: What is Virtual Fly Brain and who is it for?
results.response: Virtual Fly Brain is an interactive tool for neurobiologists to explore the detailed neuroanatomy, neuron connectivity, and gene expression of Drosophila melanogaster.

results.title: Contact / contribute
results.question: How do I report a problem or contribute data to Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: To report a problem or contribute data to Virtual Fly Brain, you can get in touch with the Virtual Fly Brain team through their contact page. For help with using Virtual Fly Brain, you can use the public support forum at support@virtualflybrain.org. To report technical issues, bugs, or request new features, you can use GitHub Issues. For data inclusion discussions, collaboration proposals, or confidential matters that require direct communication with the team, you can use the private email data@virtualflybrain.org.

results.title: Website how-to: 3D Viewer
results.question: How do I use the 3D Viewer on the VFB website?
results.response: To use the 3D Viewer on the VFB website, point and click to select neurons or expression. Click and drag with the mouse or use the directional icons to rotate or move the view. Use the zoom icons or scroll with the mouse to zoom in or out. The camera icon starts or stops a rotation animation of the scene, and the sphere icon toggles wireframes on or off.

results.title: Website how-to: Circuit Browser
results.question: What is the Circuit Browser tab on VFB and how do I use it?
results.response: The Circuit Browser allows you to find the strongest paths from one neuron to another. To use it, you would find one neuron to be the source neuron and another to be the target neuron.

results.title: Concepts: NBLAST
results.question: What is NBLAST and what does an NBLAST similarity score mean?
results.response: NBLAST is a method used to calculate similarity scores. An NBLAST similarity score represents the morphological similarity between neurons or expression patterns. The similarity scores are calculated using NBLAST.

results.title: Concepts: confidence values
results.question: What do confidence values mean on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: VFB's documentation does not appear to cover confidence values. Searching virtualflybrain.org may provide more information on this topic.

results.title: Concepts: bridging registrations
results.question: What are bridging registrations between brain templates in VFB?
results.response: VFB's documentation does not appear to cover bridging registrations between brain templates. The available information describes various queries and datasets aligned to the [adult brain template JFRC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00017894 "Open adult brain template JFRC2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), including painted domains, images, and datasets, but does not mention bridging registrations.

results.title: Data coverage & templates
results.question: What imaging data types and brain templates does Virtual Fly Brain hold?
results.response: Virtual Fly Brain holds various imaging data types and brain templates. It integrates neuroanatomical and expression data from the published literature, as well as image datasets, onto the same brain template.

results.title: API: REST endpoints
results.question: How can I query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API?
results.response: You can query Virtual Fly Brain programmatically using the SOLR or Owlery API. The Owlery API provides OWL reasoning services for Virtual Fly Brain's ontologies, enabling complex queries over class hierarchies and relationships. The SOLR Search API provides fast text search and autocomplete functionality for Virtual Fly Brain entities, datasets, and publications. To use the Owlery API, access the API Endpoint at https://owl.virtualflybrain.org/ and use various operations such as Knowledgebase Operations, DL Queries, and SPARQL Services.

results.title: Anatomy teaching diagrams
results.question: Is there a circuit diagram of the mushroom body available on Virtual Fly Brain?
results.response: There is a schematic representation of the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") available on Virtual Fly Brain, which shows the compartmental organisation of the [adult mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003684 "Open adult mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") lobes, including how the dendrites of mushroom body output neurons and the axon terminals of dopaminergic neurons tile the lobes into a stereotyped grid of 15 compartments.
